# Exact S-matrices of the simply-laced theories {#sec-simply-laced}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- Build the S-matrices of the simply-laced theories from the blocks $(x)$ and $\{x\}$.
- Check unitarity, crossing and the bootstrap, and read the bound states off the poles.
- Derive the S-matrices for every simply-laced algebra from Dorey's root-system formula.
- Understand strong–weak duality $\beta\to4\pi/\beta$.
:::

For each simply-laced algebra there is an exact, diagonal S-matrix that satisfies all the axioms of @sec-integrable-qft, agrees with perturbation theory, and depends on the coupling only through a single parameter $B$. It was found in 1990 by three groups [@braden1990; @christe1990; @klassen1990], and Dorey [-@dorey1991] then gave a single formula for all of them in terms of the Coxeter element. This chapter presents these S-matrices.

## Building blocks {#sec-blocks}

Fix the Coxeter number $h$ and set

$$
(x)=\frac{\sinh\left(\frac\theta2+\frac{i\pi x}{2h}\right)}{\sinh\left(\frac\theta2-\frac{i\pi x}{2h}\right)},\qquad
\{x\}=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{(x-1+B)(x+1-B)} ,
$$ {#eq-blocks}

with the coupling-dependent parameter

$$
B(\beta)=\frac1{2\pi}\frac{\beta^2}{1+\beta^2/4\pi}\in[0,2) .
$$ {#eq-b-of-beta}

The block $(x)$ has a simple pole at $\theta=i\pi x/h$ and a zero at $\theta=-i\pi x/h$. It satisfies $(x)(-\theta)=(x)^{-1}$, $(0)=1$, $(h)=-1$, $(x+2h)=(x)$ and $(x)(i\pi-\theta)=-(h-x)(\theta)$. These are identities between functions of $\theta$: $(0)$ and $(h)$ are the constant functions $1$ and $-1$, not values of a block at a particular rapidity. The combination $\{x\}$ has the following properties (@exr-block-identities).

- **Unitarity and real analyticity:** $\{x\}(\theta)\{x\}(-\theta)=1$, and $\{x\}$ is a phase for real $\theta$.
- **Crossing:** $\{x\}(i\pi-\theta)=\{h-x\}(\theta)$.
- **Free limit:** at $B=0$, $\{x\}=1$.
- **Duality:** $\{x\}$ is invariant under $B\to2-B$.
- **Poles and zeros:** in the physical strip, $\{x\}$ has simple poles at $\theta=i\pi(x\pm1)/h$, independent of the coupling, and zeros at $\theta=i\pi(x-1+B)/h$ and $i\pi(x+1-B)/h$, which move with the coupling.

The numerator $(x-1)(x+1)$ is the **minimal** part. It carries the poles and depends only on $h$. The denominator is a CDD factor (@sec-cdd): it adds zeros, not poles, so it does not change the bound-state structure, and it carries all the dependence on the coupling. For $h=2$, $\{1\}=f_{-B/2}$ is the sinh-Gordon S-matrix (-@eq-sinh-gordon-smatrix).

## The $a_n^{(1)}$ S-matrices {#sec-an-smatrix}

For $a_n^{(1)}$, with $h=n+1$ and the particles labelled by $a=1,\dots,n$ so that $m_a=2m\sin\frac{\pi a}h$,

$$
S_{ab}(\theta)=\prod_{\substack{p=\lvert a-b\rvert+1\\\text{step }2}}^{a+b-1}\{p\} .
$$ {#eq-an-smatrix}

**Example: $a_2^{(1)}$.** There are two particles of equal mass, $2$ being the antiparticle of $1$, and

$$
S_{11}=S_{22}=\{1\},\qquad S_{12}=\{2\}.
$$

$S_{11}$ has a pole at $\theta=2\pi i/3$ from the block $(2)$: the bound state $1+1\to\bar1=2$ at the fusing angle of an equilateral mass triangle. $S_{12}=\{2\}$ has a pole at $\theta=i\pi/3$, its crossed image. The bootstrap $S_{12}(\theta)=S_{11}(\theta-\frac{i\pi}3)S_{11}(\theta+\frac{i\pi}3)$ holds (@exr-a2-bootstrap).

For $a\ne b$ and $a+b<h$, $S_{ab}$ has simple poles at $\theta=i\pi(a+b)/h$, the fusing $a+b\to a+b$, and at $\theta=i\pi\lvert a-b\rvert/h$, the crossed image of the fusing $a+\bar b$, and double poles at the positions in between where consecutive blocks overlap. The double poles are the anomalous thresholds of @sec-coleman-thun. For $a+b>h$ use $S_{ab}=S_{h-a,h-b}$, so that the $s$-channel pole is at $i\pi(2h-a-b)/h$.

## Dorey's formula {#sec-dorey-formula}

For a general simply-laced algebra, Dorey's root-system construction (@sec-dorey-rule) gives the S-matrix directly. With the bicoloured Coxeter element $w=s_{\rm black}s_{\rm white}$, the colours $c(a)=\pm1$ (white $=+1$), the fundamental weights $\vec\lambda_a$ and $\vec\gamma_b=(1-w^{-1})\vec\lambda_b$,

$$
S_{ab}(\theta)=\prod_{p=1}^h\Big\{2p-1+\tfrac12\big(c(b)-c(a)\big)\Big\}^{-\frac12\vec\lambda_a\cdot w^p\vec\gamma_b} ,
$$ {#eq-dorey-formula}

where blocks with $x>h$ are reduced using $\{x+2h\}=\{x\}$ and $\{-x\}=\{x\}^{-1}$. The individual exponents are half-integers, and after this reduction they combine into integer powers of the blocks. For $A_2$, $S_{11}$ has exponents $\tfrac12,0,-\tfrac12$ on $\{1\},\{3\},\{5\}$, and $\{5\}=\{-1\}=\{1\}^{-1}$ gives $S_{11}=\{1\}^{1/2}\{1\}^{1/2}=\{1\}$. This reproduces (-@eq-an-smatrix) for $a_n^{(1)}$, and for the lightest particle of $e_8^{(1)}$ it gives

$$
S_{11}=\{1\}\{11\}\{19\}\{29\},\qquad h=30 .
$$

Its poles at $\theta=\frac{2\pi i}3$, $\frac{2\pi i}5$ and $\frac{i\pi}{15}$ are the fusings $1+1\to1$, $1+1\to2$ and $1+1\to3$, with $m_2=2m_1\cos\frac\pi5$ and $m_3=2m_1\cos\frac\pi{30}$. The minimal part of the $e_8^{(1)}$ S-matrix is Zamolodchikov's S-matrix of the Ising model in a magnetic field [@zamolodchikov1989].

The signs and the direction of the colour shift in (-@eq-dorey-formula) matter. Products of blocks are easily written that are unitary, crossing symmetric and satisfy the bootstrap at every fusing, yet are not the S-matrices of the theory: the variant with $w^{-p}$ in place of $w^p$ is an example. What singles out the physical S-matrix is agreement with the known cases and with perturbation theory. All three properties, the bootstrap at every fusing of $e_7^{(1)}$ and $e_8^{(1)}$ (112 and 224 fusings respectively), and the reduction to (-@eq-an-smatrix) are checked in `textbook_code/smatrix_simply_laced.py`.

## Strong–weak duality {#sec-strong-weak}

Because every block is invariant under $B\to2-B$, so is every simply-laced S-matrix. In terms of the coupling,

$$
B\Big(\frac{4\pi}\beta\Big)=2-B(\beta) ,
$$

so the theory at coupling $\beta$ has the same S-matrix as the theory at $4\pi/\beta$. Perturbation theory in $\beta$ and in $4\pi/\beta$ describe the same physics, and the S-matrix is most strongly coupled at the self-dual point $\beta^2=4\pi$, $B=1$. This weak–strong duality of the simply-laced theories is a simple instance of the more interesting duality of the non-simply-laced theories, where the strong-coupling limit of one theory is the weak-coupling limit of the theory of the dual algebra $\hat g^\vee$ (@sec-non-simply-laced).

At $B\to0$ and $B\to2$ every block $\{x\}$ tends to 1 (the blocks $(x)$ do not depend on $B$ and do not): the theory becomes free in both limits. In between, the masses (in the normalization of @sec-one-loop-masses-real) keep their classical ratios exactly.

## Summary: the real-coupling S-matrices {#sec-real-coupling}

**Simply-laced algebras.** The S-matrices are products of building blocks

$$
\{x\}=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{(x-1+B)(x+1-B)},\qquad (x)=\frac{\sinh\left(\frac\theta2+\frac{i\pi x}{2h}\right)}{\sinh\left(\frac\theta2-\frac{i\pi x}{2h}\right)},\qquad B(\beta)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\frac{\beta^2}{1+\beta^2/4\pi},
$$

constructed by Braden, Corrigan, Dorey and Sasaki, Christe and Mussardo, and Klassen and Melzer (all 1990), with a universal root-system formula due to Dorey [@dorey1991].

**Non-simply-laced algebras.** S-matrices were proposed by Delius, Grisaru and Zanon [-@dgz1992] and by Corrigan, Dorey and Sasaki [-@corrigan1993]. They are conjectures, with the evidence listed in @sec-nsl-status. Here the Coxeter number "floats" with the coupling, between the Coxeter number $h$ of $\hat g$ and the number that plays its role in the classical masses of the dual theory $\hat g^\vee$ (@tbl-floating-h). The S-matrices of a dual pair are exchanged under strong–weak duality, in the coroot form of @sec-affine-folding.

**Checks.** These S-matrices have been checked at one loop [@braden1990; @dgz1992] and more recently by tree-level and loop integrability arguments [@dorey_polvara2022], and the coupling dependence of the mass ratio predicted for the dual pair $g_2^{(1)}/d_4^{(3)}$ has been confirmed by Monte Carlo simulation [@watts_weston1992; @beccaria1996].

**Further results.** Further [Established] results include:

- thermodynamic Bethe ansatz [@zamolodchikov1990; @klassen1990];
- form factors [@fring1993];
- the exact mass–coupling relation [@fateev1994];
- ODE/IM descriptions [@lukyanov2010; @dorey2013; @ito2014].

**Rigour.** What is known about a rigorous construction of these theories is summarized in @sec-rigorous-real.

## Exercises {#sec-simply-laced-exercises}

::: {#exr-block-identities}
Prove the properties of $(x)$ and $\{x\}$ listed in @sec-blocks. In particular, show $(x)(i\pi-\theta)=-(h-x)(\theta)$ and deduce $\{x\}(i\pi-\theta)=\{h-x\}(\theta)$.
:::

::: {#exr-a2-bootstrap}
For $a_2^{(1)}$ the only fusings are $1+1\to2$ and $2+2\to1$. Verify the bootstrap equations $S_{d2}(\theta)=S_{d1}(\theta-\frac{i\pi}3)S_{d1}(\theta+\frac{i\pi}3)$ for $d=1,2$.
:::

::: {#exr-an-poles}
For $a_n^{(1)}$, find all poles of $S_{ab}$ in the physical strip, their orders, and identify the simple poles with fusings $a+b\to a+b$ and their crossed images.
:::

::: {#exr-e8-poles}
For $e_8^{(1)}$, use the masses of @sec-masses-couplings to verify that the poles of $S_{11}=\{1\}\{11\}\{19\}\{29\}$ at $\theta=\frac{2\pi i}3,\frac{2\pi i}5,\frac{i\pi}{15}$ give the bound states $1$, $2$, $3$. Where are the other three poles, and what are they?
:::

::: {#exr-dual}
Show that $B(4\pi/\beta)=2-B(\beta)$, and that $B$ is monotonic in $\beta$ with $B(0)=0$, $B(\infty)=2$.
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-simply-laced-notes}

The simply-laced S-matrices were found by Braden, Corrigan, Dorey and Sasaki [-@braden1990], Christe and Mussardo [-@christe1990] and Klassen and Melzer [-@klassen1990]. Dorey's formula is in [@dorey1991], and Fring and Olive [@fring1992] proved uniformly, from Coxeter-element identities, that Dorey's formula satisfies crossing and the bootstrap. The $e_8$ S-matrix of the Ising model in a magnetic field is due to Zamolodchikov [-@zamolodchikov1989]. Dorey's lectures [-@dorey1998] give a detailed account of all of this.
